_exec_summary.SummaryText:
RMP Executive Summary:

This Executive Summary reviews the major elements of the Risk Management Plan (RMP) for the Cardinal FG Company flat glass manufacturing facility located in Durant, Oklahoma (Cardinal FG).  This summary is presented in response to the requirements of the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) under Title 40 of the Code of Federal Regulations, Part 68 (40 CFR 68) and Section 112(r) of the Clean Air Act.  

At Cardinal FG, our commitment to the environment Is a part of everything we do. Responsible environmental stewardship is our goal and we are engaged in developing ways to reduce our environmental footprint. We do this by producing products in accordance with not just the letter of local and national environmental laws, but also the spirit. We also take a leadership role in creating products that actually reduce usage or our collective national energy resources.

1. Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies 
Cardinal FG is committed to protecting the environment and operating facilities in a manner that promotes the safety of employees and the general public.  The design and construction of the facility has incorporated physical and operational safeguards to prevent accidental releases.  Through the proper design, installation, operation and maintenance of the equipment, and the training of our personnel, Cardinal FG has minimized the hazard to human health and the environment from fires, explosions, or any unplanned sudden or non-sudden release of hazardous materials.  

The facility relies on outside services, Emergency Management System, Fire, Police to respond to major release events.  In the event that a release does occur, the facility's emergency response is described in its emergency action plan.  The emergency action plan includes procedures to provide information to and coordinate response actions with local emergency response personnel (i.e., law enforcement, fire, and rescue departments, emergency

medical services, hospital and government personnel, etc.) as well as any potentially affected neighbors.  In addition, the emergency action plan is used to familiarize local emergency response personnel with the types of material handled and internal emergency response procedures.

2. Facility Description and Regulated Substances Handled
Cardinal FG is a flat glass manufacturing facility using the tin bath flotation process. The facility is subject to the RMP rule due to the storage of sulfur dioxide, a regulated toxic substance, above the threshold quantities. 

3. Accidental Release Prevention Program and Chemical-Specific Prevention Steps
Cardinal FG has programs in place to address accidental release prevention measures required by EPA, process safety management (PSM) requirements from the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), and notification requirements of EPA's Emergency Response and Community Right-to-Know regulations.  The facility complies with PSM for the management of sulfur dioxide.

Employee Participation
Cardinal FG has developed an employee participation program.  All process safety information, process hazard analysis (PHA) results, recommendations, and action items, incident investigations, compliance audits, operating procedures, emergency response plan, and records of management of change are available to the operating personnel.

Process Hazard Analysis and Process Safety Information
The facility utilizes the What If PHA methodology.  The PHA identified the following potential major hazards: toxic release, over pressurization, corrosion, and equipment failure.  The facility utilizes process controls including vents, relief vents, check valves, manual shutoffs, alarms and procedures and emergency power to prevent or limit releases.  

Cardinal FG keeps a variety of technical documents that are used to help maintain safe operation of the facility.  The facility also maintains technical documents that provide information about th

e design and construction of process equipment. 

Operating Procedures and Training
Cardinal FG maintains written procedures that address process operations. The facility has developed and implemented a training program for all employees involved in facility operations.  

Contractors
The contractor safety procedures establish minimum guidelines and activities in order to assure that the contractor's employees follow safe work practices and procedures.  The procedure includes a contractor screening process and hazard awareness, safety and emergency procedures training.

Mechanical Integrity
The facility's mechanical integrity program includes written procedures, training, and regular inspections and equipment testing procedures to maintain piping systems, relief systems,  emergency shutdown systems, and controls in a safe operating condition.  

Management of Change
The facility's management of change (MOC) program reviews all proposed changes to process chemicals, technology, equipment, procedures, materials, and design conditions prior to implementation of the change.  Changes are reviewed to ensure that adequate controls are in place to manage any new hazards, and to verify that existing controls have not been compromised by a process change.  

Incident Investigation
Cardinal FG has procedures to promptly investigate any incident that has resulted in, or could reasonably result in a release of a regulated substance.  The procedure establishes the minimum guidelines and activities of the incident investigation program in order to reduce the likelihood of repetitive occurrences of events which could reasonably lead to catastrophic releases.  Investigations will be undertaken to identify the situation leading to the incident as well as any corrective actions to prevent a similar release in the future.

Compliance Audits
The facility conducts audits of the provisions of RMP to verify that procedures and practices developed under the standard are adequate and are bei

ng followed.  The audits include a review of documentation and process safety information, inspection of the physical facilities, and interviews with all levels of plant personnel.

4. Accident History
The facility has not had any RMP reportable accidents.  

5. Emergency Response Program
Cardinal FG maintains a written emergency response program in its emergency action plan.  The purpose of the emergency action plan is to protect worker and public safety as well as the environment.  The emergency action plan addresses aspects of emergency response, including proper first-aid and medical treatment for exposures, evacuation plans and accounting for personnel after an evacuation, notification of local emergency response agencies and the public if a release occurs, and post-incident cleanup and decontamination requirements.  In addition, Cardinal FG has procedures that address maintenance, inspection, and testing of emergency response equipment, as well as instructions that address the use of emergency response equipment.  Employees receive training in these procedures as necessary to perform their specific emergency response duties.  We work with the local fire department and emergency responders to ensure the proper execution of our plan.  The emergency response program will be updated when necessary based on modifications made to facility processes. 

6. Planned Changes to Improve Safety
The Cardinal FG facility has been designed and constructed to meet existing construction and process safety requirements. Cardinal FG will continue to evaluate and implement changes as necessary to improve safety at the facility.
